newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-LANCS DUO PILE ON THE RUNS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LANCS DUO PILE ON THE RUNS.

text.p: An unbroken stand of 243 between current England man John Crawley and former international Neil Fairbrother put Lancashire in command on the first day of their four-day English county championship match against struggling Sussex on Wednesday.
Crawley (112) and Fairbrother (132) finished the day unbeaten as Lancs closed on 380 for five.
Another England player turned on the style just when it was needed as Kent's Mark Ealham blazed 96 not out after his side had been reduced to 162 for six by Leicestershire.
Ealham, who put on 145 with Zimbabwean Paul Strang (82) saw Kent to a total of 356 for seven.
Gloucestershire's England bowling hopeful Mike Smith took six for 47 as bottom club Derbyshire were skittled for 120.
Gloucestershire swept past the meagre total to finish on 306 for four with Australian Shaun Young unbeaten on 156.
Warwickshire managed 328 for nine against Nottinghamshire at Trent Bridge despite 18-year-old seamer Paul Franks taking a hat-trick.
Franks, who finished with four for 81, is the youngest ever Notts bowler to achieve the feat and the first since Richard Hadlee in 1987.
Young opener David Roberts gave struggling Northamptonshire a lift against second-placed Essex, hitting a century in only his second championship match.
With table-topping Glamorgan facing Australia and third-placed Middlesex not playing, Essex's hopes of making ground were hit by Roberts' 117 in Northants' total of 354 for nine.

There were no hundreds for Surrey against Hampshire at Guildford despite the home side rattling up a huge first-day score of 457 for nine. England's Alec Stewart fell two short on 98 with fellow England men Mark Butcher (69) and Graham Thorpe (84) as well as captain Adam Hollioake (75) and Chris Lewis (66 not out) also in the runs.
Yorkshire bundled Durham out for just 152 with Darren Gough (four for 37) and Peter Hartley (three for 29) doing most of the damage. Yorkshire ended on 137 for two.
